clue.text: Celebrity companion you initially found to be rather formal

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: a celebrity is a star
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
first letter of you

explanation.surface: Someone meeting a famous person's partner finds them rather stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour, a British honour, and a crossword stock for companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Starchy describes stiff, prim behaviour, as stiff as a starched collar.

clue.text: Joint best team

blocks.note: the best is the top
a sports side is a team

explanation.surface: A combined squad made of the very finest players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like an adjective meaning shared; it is a noun, a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Topside is a lean cut of beef from the upper thigh, sold as a roasting joint.

clue.text: Calls for items of jewellery

blocks.note: first meaning: telephones someone
second meaning: bands worn on fingers

explanation.surface: Someone demands jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for phoning someone and the plural of a finger band worn as ornament.

clue.text: Cast  given guidance after distress

indicators.note: after says which piece comes second in the sequence

blocks.note: pain or anguish
past tense of lead, to guide

explanation.surface: Actors in a play receive direction after a difficult time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the actors in a show; it is the verb, meaning thrown.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurtle something is to fling it with great force, so a thing hurtled was thrown.

clue.text: Platitude from old male hugged by lady at wedding

indicators.note: being hugged means being held inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: the woman getting married
O for old and M for male

explanation.surface: An elderly man, embraced by the bride at the reception, offers a tired cliché.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is a common crossword shorthand: O for old and M for male. Bromide was once a sedative, hence a dull, calming remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A bromide, named after the old sedative, is a trite and soothing remark, a commonplace saying.

clue.text: Remember taking everyone to the sports ground

indicators.note: taking one thing to another sets them side by side in order

blocks.note: rec is British informal for a recreation ground, a public park for games
all people

explanation.surface: Someone remembers taking the whole gang down to the playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall something is to bring it back to mind, a direct synonym of remember.

clue.text: Princess entertained by the most peculiar church member

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, so these words are read in a strange new order
a guest entertained by a host is taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: seven letters of fodder
Diana, Princess of Wales, known as Di

explanation.surface: A princess is hosted by the oddest member of a congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the most into METHOST, then put DI inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Methodist belongs to the Protestant denomination founded by John Wesley, a church member.

clue.text: Ice does melt, see!

indicators.note: melting loses shape, so these letters re-form in a new arrangement

blocks.note: seven letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Someone points out ice thawing: look!
explanation.walkthrough: 'see!' reads as look; it is the noun, a bishop's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the area under a bishop's authority, which is another name for a bishop's district.

clue.text: Extreme characters from Athens?

blocks.note: surface reading: wild, outlandish people from the Greek capital
setter's reading: the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: Characters means letters, and extreme means at either end; Athens points to Greek script.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the opening and closing Greek letters, used to mean the beginning and end of everything.

clue.text: Nothing by writer accessible?

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces are set side by side

blocks.note: zero looks like the letter O
a pen is a writing tool

explanation.surface: A question of whether a writer with no output is approachable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open can be entered or reached freely, without barriers or restriction.

clue.text: Oriental Co restructured, moving to a new place

indicators.note: a firm that is restructured is reorganised, so these letters get rearranged

blocks.note: ten letters of fodder

explanation.surface: An Eastern company reorganises itself and shifts to new premises.
explanation.definitionFit: Relocation is the act of shifting home or business premises somewhere else, used here as a noun phrase.

clue.text: Girl, a learner, getting book in church

blocks.note: a miss is a young woman
taken as written
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A young female student is handed a book at church.
explanation.definitionFit: A missal is the book containing the texts used in celebrating Catholic Mass throughout the year.

clue.text: Blessed with a word of greeting one day in the middle of the week

blocks.note: a variant spelling of hello

blocks.clueFragment: one day in the middle of the week
blocks.note: short for Wednesday, the midweek day

explanation.surface: Someone greeted on a Wednesday feels blessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed means made holy or consecrated, treated as sacred.

clue.text: Heed bairn in trouble in part of Scotland

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase: belonging to that region

indicators.note: letters in trouble are thrown into disorder and must be rearranged

blocks.note: nine letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Pay attention to a Scottish child who has got into bother somewhere in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: A bairn is a Scots word for a child, fitting the Scottish scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebridean means from the Hebrides, the island chains off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Updating course in divinity given to new undergraduate

indicators.note: given to means added on, so the pieces are joined in order

blocks.note: RE is religious education, the British school subject
fresher is British for a first-year university student

explanation.surface: A first-year student is offered a course in theology.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher is a short training session that brings someone's skills or knowledge up to date.

clue.text: More than one tree languishes

blocks.note: first meaning: plural of a conifer
second meaning: wastes away from longing

explanation.surface: A grove of trees that seem to droop and wither.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the plural of a needle-leaved conifer and a verb for yearning or wasting away.

clue.text: Boss almost making a tactless remark

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: gaffer is British slang for a boss or foreman

explanation.surface: The boss nearly puts their foot in it with an awkward comment.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaffer is informal British for boss; lose its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder, an embarrassing slip said or done without thinking.

clue.text: Poisonous plant — it is buried in a geometric shape

indicators.note: something buried in is put deep inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: A plus cone, a solid shape
taken as written

explanation.surface: A toxic plant lies hidden inside a geometric figure.
explanation.walkthrough: IT goes inside A CONE: ACON-IT-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, also called monkshood or wolfsbane, is a highly toxic flowering herb.

clue.text: Supplement when cold is caught becoming a habit

indicators.note: something caught is trapped inside, so this letter goes within the other piece

blocks.note: an extra or add-on
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Taking a supplement whenever you catch a cold turns into a habit.
explanation.definitionFit: An addiction is a compulsive dependency, a habit someone cannot easily break.

clue.text: India has wise man with lines offering pictorial language

blocks.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a mage is a learned man or magician
RY for railway, lines of track

explanation.surface: A wise man in India speaks in vivid, picture-filled verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagery is descriptive writing that evokes mental pictures, figurative or visual language.

clue.text: Instrument needs circular aperture — then air can get circulated

indicators.note: things circulated are passed around, so these letters are mixed up

blocks.note: a round hole looks like the letter O
six letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A wind instrument needs a round hole so that air can flow through it.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes, a musical instrument.

clue.text: Map book arrives on time in the end

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the first piece comes before the second

blocks.note: a book of maps
T for time

explanation.surface: A book of maps finally turns up punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means finally, after a long wait, which is what in the end conveys.

clue.text: Impetus bringing hesitation after a little while

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other in the sequence

blocks.note: a short space of time
the filler sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A short pause and an um can stall the drive of a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentum is driving force or impetus gained by motion, the push that keeps things going.

clue.text: Marian trained to be a pilot, perhaps

indicators.note: trained suggests being drilled into a new shape, so the name's letters are reordered

blocks.note: six letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A woman named Marian goes through training to fly planes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is one example of an airman, a member of an air force or any aviator; hence perhaps.

clue.text: Flighty type gettin' dressed?

blocks.note: first meaning: a small bird, a creature of flight
second meaning: putting on robes, with the final g dropped as the apostrophe shows

explanation.surface: A frivolous person is putting their clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty' suggests fickle, but here it means able to fly; the dropped g in gettin' tells you to drop it from the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-breasted garden bird flies, and robing without its final g reads robin'.

clue.text: Correct perspective for seeing something trigonometrical

blocks.note: correct means right
a point of view or slant

explanation.surface: Getting the proper viewpoint on a problem of maths.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninety-degree corner is the basis of triangle calculations in trigonometry, hence something trigonometrical.

clue.text: Enticement that gets one into club

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it

blocks.note: a club used to strike a ball
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lure that persuades someone to join a members' club.
explanation.definitionFit: Bait is a lure, food or a temptation used to draw a fish or a person in.

clue.text: Hide discharge

blocks.note: first meaning: conceal, stress on the second syllable
second meaning: produce and release a substance, as a gland does

explanation.walkthrough: Two verbs from different roots share one spelling: one from secret, one from secretion.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to conceal something away and, biologically, for a gland to release a fluid.

clue.text: Many sadly facing ruin in Asian country

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled
facing means set up front of the next piece

blocks.note: four letters of fodder
to mar is to spoil

explanation.surface: Many people sadly face devastation in a troubled Asian nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Myanmar, formerly Burma, is a nation in Southeast Asia bordering Thailand and Bangladesh.
